targetAudience.primary: Engineers designing resumable digital employees and nested human-in-the-loop workflows
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands checkpoints, tool calls, branches and replay.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A restored checkpoint can attach a late answer to the wrong call or replay work whose effect is uncertain.

whyNow: A same-day merged Google ADK Python change demonstrates typed continuation decisions, whole-component branch identity and nested replay beyond a fixed event window.

externalHook.description: Nested answers are bound through call and branch identity before the runtime chooses continue, pause or replay.

coreProposition: Safe continuation requires a compound authority identity that binds workflow frame, call occurrence, branch identity, responder evidence and known effect state; robust event matching can decide pause, replay or continue, but it cannot authenticate the responder or prove exactly-once external effects.

originalValue.description: Elevates continuation from state restoration to a compound authority identity and separates event-history correctness from responder and effect authorization.

readerTakeaway: Persist frame, call, branch, responder and effect identities separately; allow replay only when the live frame and effect evidence justify it.

supported: The implementation expresses continue, pause and replay as typed decisions.
Whole run-id components and branch relationships bind nested responses.
Tests cover historical pauses, parallel calls, unrelated branches and replay.
uncertain: Which effect receipt makes non-idempotent replay safe

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument is a general continuation-governance pattern.

decisionReason: The merged implementation and regression matrix support a concrete continuation mechanism and a distinct evidence-bounded authority model.
